The encoding does not implement the disability-benefit-computation-year branch in §415(b)(2)(A)(ii), including its continuing-applicability rule; listing a deferred output does not make the otherwise-computing module safe for the whole cited slice.

It treats the statutorily required selection of the highest adjusted earnings among computation base years as an opaque `sum_top_n_over_periods` input, rather than encoding the defined benefit-computation-years selection and the applicable computation-base-year exclusions.
The elapsed-years formula can use a death year before 1961 as the endpoint, although §415(b)(2)(B)(iii) qualifies the earlier-death endpoint as occurring after 1960.
The old-age/death computation does not model the distinct statutory computation-base-year endpoints for first old-age entitlement and death, instead relying on a combined sentinel input.

[non-blocking] The supplied tests cover indexed versus unindexed earnings and one death scenario, but do not exercise the statutory minimum of two years, the post-1960 death qualification, or meaningful inapplicability boundaries.
